description.narrative:
Project Description
The Ghanaian Smart SDG Cities Initiative builds on Norway’s previous support to the Ministry of Finance to advance the achievement of Smart Sustainable Development Goals (Smart SDGs) in Ghana. In keeping with UN Habitat’s SDG Cities initiative, it accelerates the achievement of SDGs in cities through systematic processes of data collection and analysis; developing city development strategies that incorporate Smart SDG cities approaches; strengthening key local institutional capacities in areas of planning, governance, revenue and service delivery as key to promoting sustainable urban development; advancing the implementation of high impact local initiatives through supporting their preparation and financing; and over all providing awareness and education on smart SDG challenges and solution to the inhabitants, particularly women and youth. Eventually the Cities are recognized for their exceptional achievements through SDG Cities Certification. Project Approach
Overview: The initiative advances the achievement of SDGs in cities through systematic processes of data collection and analysis; development of city development strategies incorporating smart cities approaches; strengthening key local institutional capacities defined by the New Urban Agenda as drivers of sustainable urban development - planning, governance, finance and service delivery; and facilitating the financing of high impact local initiatives, including those that reduce the digital divide and advance smart cities. Cities are recognized for their exceptional achievements through SDG Cities Certification.
Objective: Accelerated achievement of the SDGs in cities by enhancing urban climate resilience and promoting a green transition of urban or secondary cities in Ghana with the use of digital tools
Indicators: Measurable progress on SDG achievement against their baseline assessment (60% of participating cities within 5 years of onboarding)
Outcome 1: Outcome 2: Improved support structure for accelerating SDGs in cities Improved evidence-based planning Outcome 3: Strengthened local institutions, able to effectively progress economic, social and environment dimensions of sustainable urban development through digital training resources and tools Outcome 4: Increased, measurable SDG impacts in cities
Outcome 1 is implemented through the following actions: o Continued political will on local implementation of SDGs A national Advisory Committee is established, co-chaired by Ministry of Finance (MoF) and Ministry of Local Government, and involving other institutions such as Decentralisation and Rural Development (MLGDRD), National Development Planning Commission (NDPC), Civil Society Organisations as relevant, Ghana Investment Promotion Centre, UN-Habitat, Norway´s Bærekraftnetverket and eventually the onboarded cities
o Smart SDG Cities Technical Hub established An SDG Cities Technical Hub is established in Accra with national experts in areas of data, governance, planning, revenue, urban basic services and investment.
o Cities are onboarded into Smart SDG Cities Initiative via a digital platform Through the support of the Advisory Committee participating cities are identified and onboarded. Criteria will be developed by the Advisory Committee with particular attention to women-led cities, balanced geographic distribution and a variety of population sizes. The onboarding process involves participating cities taking stock of their progress in implementing SDGs, and mayors committing to: prioritising SDGs; increasing public awareness on the SDGs including amongst women, youth and children; ensuring evidence-based, participatory, inclusive strategic planning; prioritising the implementation of SDG projects that advance SDGs and leave no one behind; and, improving the effectiveness of local institutions.
o Progress towards SDGs recognised through the SDG Cities Certification The performance of cities in generating evidence-based plans, improving local systems and capacities and ultimately driving SDG impact is recognised globally through a series of SDG Cities Certificates. The certification process will impartially assess the city's efforts to improve its SDG performance. City SDG certification will be compared despite environmental differences and help validate and systematize the effective measures to improve action performance. SDG Cities Certifications include Silver (onboarding); Gold (data/strategy); Platinum (strengthened institutions); Diamond (measurable progress).
